title: What Counts as Prepaid on a Packaged Holiday
content:
How much of the cost of the holiday counts as prepaid, when a declaration on the Travel Protection Plans is
corrected, turns on whether the final payment for that holiday has been taken and on whether its ledger carries
a penalty raised for a cancellation. Both stand on the operator's ledger for the packaged holiday held under the
Vacation Package Products.

## The three readings

1. Where the holiday's final payment has been taken and its ledger carries no penalty raised for a cancellation,
   the whole of that cost counts as prepaid.
2. Where the holiday's final payment has not been taken, only the deposit counts as prepaid.
3. In every other case the whole of that cost counts as prepaid except the charges raised for optional
   components, and the figure is never less than nothing.

The third reading is the one that answers a holiday whose final payment has been taken and whose ledger does
carry a penalty raised for a cancellation, that combination reaching neither of the first two.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A holiday costing 12400.00, of which 1500.00 stands as the deposit and 900.00 as charges for optional
components, counts as prepaid at 12400.00 under the first reading, at 1500.00 under the second, and at 11500.00
under the third. The figures are hypothetical.
